lines.en: My plan was clear.

The First Apostle—that is, the plagiarist—had ‘information from the third round and part of the fourth round,’ the early portion of Ways of Survival. And as people with information so often did, he wanted to monopolize it badly enough to hide it even from his fellow Prophets.
Meanwhile, the ‘Tyrant King,’ one of Seoul’s Seven Kings, had learned of the <Prophets> and was making use of their ‘revelations.’
One guy who wanted to monopolize information, and another who wanted to dig it out.
What would happen when the two met was plain as day.
Lee Sungkook asked.
“······So you’re saying you’ll make a text copy of the novel?”
“That’s right.”
The operation itself was simple.
Make a text copy of the plagiarist’s novel.
Then spread it among the people at each station.
Well, something along these lines should do.
―Part of the ‘revelation text’ held by the <Prophets> has been leaked!
As it happened, the groundwork was already well laid.

Thanks to Han Donghoon’s Comments Manipulation, quite a bit of information about the <Prophets> had already spread online. If word of a leaked text copy got out under those circumstances, it would cause a huge stir on the internet.
The very few early dropouts who hadn’t yet been wiped out would try to obtain the hidden pieces, and naturally, the Tyrant King who had recruited them would make his move too.
“But······ we’ve forgotten almost everything in [SSSSS-grade Infinite Regressor]. How are we supposed to make a text copy?”
“Why do we need the contents of the plagiarized work?”
“What?”
“We remember the original, don’t we?”
A brief exclamation. But Jung Minseob’s face remained troubled.
“Uh······ there’s still a problem, though. Most of the hidden pieces in ‘Ways of Survival’ that we know about have already been used up······.”

“I’ll provide the information about the hidden pieces. Let’s just mix a few things I tell you into the early part of the story as we write. We’ll only release information about items of a suitable level.”
Above all, things the plagiarist or the Tyrant King would covet.
Lee Sungkook smiled awkwardly.
“This is kind of funny. Me, making a text copy. Usually I just read them.”
These bastards······ were they illegal downloaders?
Jung Minseob chimed in too.
“But won’t doing this make us just like him? In the end, we’re making a story by plagiarizing the original······.”
He had a point.
I thought for a moment, then spoke.
“There’s a saying. Plagiarism hopes you don’t know the original, parody is more fun if you know the original, and homage hopes you’ll recognize the original.”
“Ah, that’s an interesting saying.”
“So what we’re about to do is an homage.”
It was true. I wanted lots of people to know about [SSSSS-grade Infinite Regressor].
That way, he would go down sooner.

We borrowed the laptop Gong Pildu had used and started typing. None of us had much experience writing a novel, so we had to put our heads together and discuss it. Jung Minseob spoke, pulling at his hair.
“I had no idea writing was this hard······ writers really are amazing······.”

“Let’s just write something rough. We don’t need the whole story anyway, only the information that will lure them out. In fact, the more incomplete the revelation, the easier it might be to fool the Prophets. We need to mix truth and lies in the right proportions.”
As I watched what Jung Minseob was typing, I added bits to it.
“And let’s change the characters’ names slightly. There are a few things I’m worried about.”

Characters like Lee Hyunsung and Lee Jihye could be shocked if they learned about this story. Like it or not, they would eventually find out that this world was ‘inside a novel,’ but that didn’t have to happen right now.
But Jung Minseob said something unexpected.
“Well, I don’t think you need to worry too much about that.”
“What?”

“Actually, Sungkook and I once went around telling a few characters that ‘this place is inside a novel,’ just to test it. But they didn’t understand at all. As if they were NPCs······. No matter how seriously we explained it, they just took it as a joke.”
That was another unexpected piece of information.

Come to think of it, I had seen Jung Minseob and the other <Apostles> tell characters things like ‘You’re only a supporting character’ a few times. Thinking back on the characters’ reactions then······ there certainly had been something strange about them.
Jung Minseob continued.

“That’s also why the First Apostle could identify the <Prophets> so easily. The ‘characters’ here react very badly to being told ‘this place is inside a novel,’ or act as though they haven’t heard it. I suspect that’s why the <Apostles> go out of their way to use the term ‘revelation.’”
Hearing that suddenly made me uneasy.
I spoke without thinking.
“······What’s the difference between the characters and us?”
“What? Hmm······ we’re people from reality, and the characters are people from a novel? Isn’t that about the extent of the difference?”
“Then······ when did this world become divided into reality and fiction?”
“Hmm, I’m not sure······. When the first scenario began?”
Even after Jung Minseob’s answer, my questions remained unresolved.
Lee Sungkook and Jung Minseob, standing before me, were clearly ‘outsiders’ from beyond the novel, just like me.
That was why I hadn’t been able to see their information at first either.
But after the recent update, I could examine their information through [Character List].
Then were they ‘real people’ now, or ‘characters’?
If everyone eventually became a ‘character’ as time passed······.
At that moment, I turned to look at Yoo Sangah and Lee Gilyoung, who were some distance away.
[Activating the exclusive skill ‘Character List’!]
[This person is not registered in ‘Character List’.]
[Information on this person is currently being collected.]
Fortunately, I still couldn’t see information on either of them.
Yoo Sangah happened to turn my way and smiled.
Lee Gilyoung looked at me too.
“What is it, hyung?”
“Nothing.”
I wasn’t quite sure why, but I felt strangely relieved.
Before long, we finished the rough outline of the novel.
The quality was bad enough that it would have flopped spectacularly if serialized on Textpia, but that shit didn’t matter now.
“First, let’s spread the word that the revelation text has been leaked.”
Lee Sungkook asked.
“Will there be enough time for the news to spread?”
“I’ll ask Donghoon. If he uses his [Reclusive Loner] attribute, spreading it in a short time shouldn’t be a problem.”
“Ah, if it’s Donghoon······ all right. But not every station has internet access. What do we do about those?”
“I have someone to send to those stations.”
I looked behind me.
Kang Ilhun nodded as though he had been waiting.
Lee Sungkook agreed.
“Ah, I see. If it’s Ilhun-ssi, then certainly······ goodness, I’d forgotten.”
“Kang Ilhun-ssi, you’re ready, right?”
Kang Ilhun, the former deputy representative of Dongdaemun.
It had been worth deliberately keeping this guy alive after all.
Kang Ilhun spoke with a slightly nervous expression.
“Leave it to me. I’m confident when it comes to running my mouth. All I need to do is spread the rumor, right?”
[The character ‘Kang Ilhun’ is relying on you.]
[Your understanding of this character increases.]
Kang Ilhun.
The time had finally come for his [Rumours Expert] attribute to shine.
There were now 44 hours left until the scenario ended.
Within the next day, the contest would begin.
―Donghoon, thanks.
―I’m just returning the favor, so don’t worry about it.
[The character ‘Han Donghoon’ trusts you slightly.]

After what happened last time, Han Donghoon, the ‘Hermit King of Shadows,’ had opened up to me quite a bit. Apparently, rescuing him from the clutches of the <Prophets> had meant more to him than I’d expected.
―I feel strangely close to you, hyung.
―Close?
―Like you’re someone I’ve known for a long time······ are you a ‘Reclusive Loner’ too, by any chance?
―Hmm, no, I’m not. Though I am a bit timid.
―I see. When I talk to you, hyung, I feel something like a wall I can’t quite understand. I can’t explain it very well, but I like it.
―Isn’t it usually a bad thing to feel a wall like that?
―I only trust people who have walls. I think that to understand someone, you first have to face that wall.
The kid was only seventeen, yet he talked like some sage.
A wall, though. He might well be right.
Some walls make you yearn all the more because you can’t cross them.
―Anyway, I’ve spread all the rumors. But how are you going to distribute that ‘revelation’? Through the internet again?
―No. If I spread it online, the wrong people would read it too. I’m going to sell it.
―Sell it? How?
I began explaining to Han Donghoon.
40 hours until the scenario ended.
At last, I gathered my companions in Chungmuro.
“This journey won’t be easy. If we don’t capture ‘Changsin Station’ within the next 40 hours, our group will be wiped out. And the force that currently holds that station is formidable.”
“Well, when has it ever been easy? Who are we up against this time?”
I answered Jung Heewon’s question.
“A guy called the Tyrant King. He’s currently counted among Seoul’s Seven Kings, and he has the largest territory of any king in the northern region.”
This time, Lee Hyunsung asked.
“What kind of person is he?”

“He started around Dobong-gu and has been moving south, building his own ‘kingdom.’ They say he takes anyone pretty or handsome as a concubine, regardless of whether they’re men or women, and kills the ugly ones or makes them slaves.”
Jung Heewon frowned.
“Then you’ll be a slave if you get caught, Dokja-ssi.”
“······Well, I think you’d be in danger too, Heewon-ssi.”
“Being a concubine would be a problem... How about we go kill him right away?”
“That would be difficult. His constellation sponsor is quite powerful. For now, there are two ways. Take the flag he holds, or capture ‘Dobong Station,’ his main base.”
Neither option was easy, so everyone seemed tense. I decided it was time to get to the point.
“First, we’ll go to Gwanghwamun.”
“What? Didn’t you say we were going to fight them?”
“They’ll be coming there.”
“Why?”
“I leaked some information. We need to allow time for him to make his move, so we’ll leave in a little while. Everyone, get ready in advance······ huh?”
“······What is it all of a sudden?”
At Yoo Sangah’s question, I gave a faint smile.
“Nothing. It seems things are moving faster than I expected.”
A message from Han Donghoon arrived on my smartphone.
―I told people they could search for it on the ‘Exchange.’ That’s okay, right?
―Yes, that’s right. Good job.
Then system messages came pouring into my ears, one after another.
[An item you listed on the Exchange has been sold.]
[An item you listed on the Exchange has been sold.]
Bihyung’s voice came from thin air.
[······Your attribute is Con Artist, isn’t it?]
‘How are the constellations reacting?’

[They’re incredibly excited, obviously. The filtering restrictions have started easing little by little too······ some have even gifted it directly to their incarnations. But doing this will draw attention to you again. Will you be okay? And won’t releasing information you know put you at a disadvantage too?]
‘It won’t.’
I had more information than I could use anyway.
And the information I’d released wasn’t information I needed.
Rather, it was information that would hurt someone else.
‘Just hand over the coins from the sales.’
[Here you go, you bastard.]
[16 copies of ‘Revelation Text─ SSSSS-grade Infinite Regressor’ have been sold on the Exchange.]
[You have acquired 16000 coins.]
It went without saying, but I hadn’t released the text copy for free.
Everyone who needed this information would have a contract with a constellation sponsor anyway, so selling it through the ‘Exchange’ was better than distributing it online.
Releasing a ‘revelation text’ containing important information for free would be all the more suspicious.
But what if I put a price on it and sold it?
Those who needed it would naturally buy it.
Because they would mistakenly believe the information had that much ‘value.’
Sometimes the quality of information was determined by its price rather than its contents.
16000 coins, though. This was quite lucrative.
I spoke to my companions.
“Sorry, but I’m going to take a quick nap.”
“······Aren’t you being a little too carefree?”
“Some things can only be done while sleeping.”
I settled down on the spot and lay back. Yoo Sangah covered me with a thin blanket she had brought from somewhere. Jung Heewon clicked her tongue as though she couldn’t believe it.
And I fell asleep in an instant.
A moment later, a system message sounded within my hazy consciousness.
[Activating stage 3 of the exclusive skill, ‘Omniscient Reader’s Viewpoint’.]
From what I had discovered so far, [Omniscient Reader’s Viewpoint] was divided into three stages.
Stage 1, which let me read a character’s simple actions or emotions.
Stage 2, which let me know a character’s inner thoughts.
Stage 3, which let me see the surroundings where characters were located, or immerse myself directly in a character.
So far, I had experienced stage 3 a total of two times.
Once in a dream, and once in a state of suspended animation.
In the dream, I had seen Yoo Joonghyuk leaving Geumho Station.
In suspended animation, I had witnessed the scene at Chungmuro.
Those two instances had something in common.
The fact that my consciousness had been hazy and unstable.
But that wasn’t the only condition for activating stage 3.
There was one more condition, the most important of all.
Namely.
「‘Representative-nim, are you watching? Damn it······ am I doing this right?’
Kang Ilhun, who had been muttering intently to himself, spoke while looking into empty space.
‘I’ve definitely spread the word to the Tyrant King’s side. They’ll make their move soon too. But you are listening to me, right?’」
The character in question and I had to be ‘thinking about each other’ at the same time.
A moment later, my field of vision writhed, and the scenes Kang Ilhun was spying on appeared.
「A man was smiling, baring his gleaming white teeth. Wearing a dazzling dragon robe and a peculiar gold crown, he slowly rose from his throne while the women around him attended to him.
“The new revelation?”
“It seems reliable. We bought the information with coins, so there’s no doubt about it.”
“Who released the information?”
“Probably one of the <Apostles>.”
“How trustworthy is it?”
“We checked a few hidden pieces described in the revelation text, and they were all genuine.”
The man grinned, baring his teeth.
“Let’s go to Gwanghwamun. We’ll occupy it before the others arrive.”」
Good. The Tyrant King was finally making his move.
Now there was the matter of the other side.
I thought of Jung Minseob.
「‘Representative-nim. He’s arrived.’」
Good timing too.
Jung Minseob had gone ahead to the Sejong-daero intersection in Gwanghwamun.
Soon, the scene around Jung Minseob came into view.
「‘Judging by that chuuni-looking hood he’s wearing, I’m pretty sure. It’s him.’」

Figures shifting beneath a structure. Just as I’d expected, the plagiarist had arrived first. One of the third round’s most useful hidden pieces lay concealed in Gwanghwamun. He must have been starting to shit himself by now, so he couldn’t help rushing over.
「‘The problem is, it seems they aren’t the only ones who’ve come. The kings from Yeongdeungpo, Yongsan, and Seongdong-gu seem to have made their moves too······ isn’t this getting too big?’」
No, this was exactly what I wanted.
One by one, those who had remained beneath the surface were starting to emerge.
All the better. Now I didn’t have to seek them out individually.
At last, the final act of the fourth scenario.
The ‘War of Kings’ would begin.
My consciousness quietly rises, and my senses gradually return to reality.
[Ending stage 3 of the exclusive skill, ‘Omniscient Reader’s Viewpoint’.]
Stage 3 was more exhausting than I’d expected, so I couldn’t maintain it for long.
Besides, I had discovered one disappointing fact.

Using stage 3 of [Omniscient Reader’s Viewpoint] didn’t necessarily give me a skill reward. It seemed I could only obtain that reward by entering [First-Person Protagonist’s Viewpoint], but unfortunately, I hadn’t discovered the conditions for entering it.
If only I could use [First-Person Protagonist’s Viewpoint] to swipe Yoo Joonghyuk’s skills every time I fell asleep. Nothing could be better.
When I opened my eyes and groggily sat up, Jung Heewon was watching me.
“You were talking in your sleep again.”
Talking in my sleep? No way.
“What did I say?”
“Mom······ that’s what it sounded like you were saying.”
Why had I said that to myself?
Not knowing whether it was true made this awkward.
Jung Heewon simply watched me with an inscrutable smile.
I offered a vague excuse.
“Well, I am worried about my mother too. Anyway, Jung Heewon-ssi, I have a favor to ask.”
“What is it?”
“I’d like you to sit out the battle at Gwanghwamun this time.”
“There’s something else I need you to do. And you’re the only person I can trust with it.”
At my words about trusting her, Jung Heewon stuck out her lower lip, pretending to give in reluctantly.
“I’ll hear you out first. What is it?”
After finishing my conversation with Jung Heewon, the first thing I did was decide who would remain at Chungmuro and who would head to Gwanghwamun.
“Jung Heewon-ssi has a mission, so we’ll leave her out. First, I’ll decide who will stay at Chungmuro.”
A few of my companions swallowed.
Faces like those of subjects awaiting a king’s selection.
“First, Gong Pildu-ssi and Lee Hyunsung-ssi will stay behind.”
“Hmph, you’re really working me like a slave.”
Gong Pildu snorted as though he had expected it. The problem was Lee Hyunsung. His face had gone slightly pale, and somehow he looked as though he had been passed over for promotion.

“Hyunsung-ssi, I need you to stay. We need someone to defend this place alongside Gong Pildu-ssi. Even if Chungmuro comes under attack, I’m sure you’ll be able to lead the people just as well as Yoo Sangah-ssi.”
“······Yes. Understood.”
He seemed disappointed, but it couldn’t be helped. I had my reasons for leaving that dependable Steel Sword Emperor behind.

“You already have good enough skills, Hyunsung-ssi. The problem is that their levels are too low. While we’re away, please improve your proficiency in ‘Great Mountain Smash.’ Once this scenario is over, we’ll really start needing your help.”
Only then did Lee Hyunsung brighten a little.
“Yes! Leave it to me.”
As expected, soldiers were at their most efficient when they had a manual and a fixed daily routine.
And so we set out on our journey to Gwanghwamun.
Apart from Yoo Joonghyuk and Lee Jihye, who were moving separately, there were four core members: me, Yoo Sangah, Lee Gilyoung, and Lee Sungkook.
The group members at Chungmuro waved as they watched us leave.
“Deputy Representative-nim! Have a safe trip!”
“Please stay safe!”
It had only been a few days, yet Yoo Sangah’s popularity was already sky-high.
A lot of people must have grown attached to Yoo Sangah in that short time; they all looked worried. Yet Yoo Sangah herself looked anxious as she left.
“Dokja-ssi, will I be any help?”
Apparently, it was time for another round of self-deprecation.
At times like this, I had to tell her plainly, even if it hurt her feelings.
“Yoo Sangah-ssi. If you keep acting like that, you’re being a burden.”
“You’re more than capable, Yoo Sangah-ssi. Have you ever seen me bring someone along for no reason?”
“Of course I trust you, Dokja-ssi, but I don’t know whether I’ll be as helpful as Hyunsung-ssi or Heewon-ssi······.”
“You can do things those two can’t, Yoo Sangah-ssi. You’re essential to this plan.”
After I emphasized it again, Yoo Sangah’s expression softened a little. Yoo Sangah really was talented. If only she had confidence.
“You said before that you had a Korean history certificate, right?”
“Oh, yes.”
Perhaps because we were talking about the past, Yoo Sangah’s face brightened considerably. But only for a moment; she soon grew glum again.
“······Though it’s useless now.”
“It is useful. That’s why I brought you along.”
Originally, I hadn’t intended to give Yoo Sangah this role.
There was another suitable person if we went down toward Gwangjin-gu.
But we had no time to go looking for that person, and someone of Yoo Sangah’s caliber would be more than enough.
The Yoo Sangah I knew was smart enough to memorize the whole of Korean history from beginning to end just to earn a level 1 Korean history certificate.
“You remember the Samyeongdang statue from last time, right?”
“Yes.”
“There should be several similar things on the way to Gwanghwamun. There’s a national museum in that area, and quite a few sacred statues too.”
As expected, Yoo Sangah understood at once and exclaimed.
“Ah! I see. Come to think of it, other relics and historic sites could hold the power of constellations too.”
“Yes. Your mission this time is to find those relics and historic sites, Yoo Sangah-ssi.”
“Understood! I’ll put my brain to work.”
“The more obscure the things left behind by famous people, the better.”
Even among Historical-grade constellations, their power varied enormously depending on their fame.
The difference between Samyeongdang and the Duke of Loyalty and Warfare alone made that clear.

Items left by Samyeongdang were B-grade, but in the case of things like the Twin Dragon Swords left by the Duke of Loyalty and Warfare, even those not meant for actual combat had a quality around S-grade.
“We need to collect as many items as possible on the way to Gwanghwamun. Our numbers are relatively small.”
The Tyrant King had probably brought hundreds of incarnations with him.
The plagiarist would have a force of his own too.
We also had to watch out for the kings coming up from Yeongdeungpo, Yongsan, and Seongdong-gu.
I had a rough idea of who they might be, but the butterfly effect could have changed history.
Just then, Yoo Sangah clapped her hands.
“Ah, now that I think about it, there’s a place that comes to mind.”
“What?”
“I’m not sure if I remember correctly······ but there should be a Gwanseongmyo (關聖廟) shrine somewhere near here.”
“Gwanseongmyo?”
“Yes. It might hold the spiritual power of a great historical figure, so wouldn’t it be worth stopping by on the way? Though not a Korean historical figure······.”
Not a Korean historical figure?
Gwanseongmyo. Even I, an avid reader of ‘Ways of Survival,’ had never heard of such a place.
Anyway, we decided to follow Yoo Sangah’s suggestion and travel aboveground.
How long had we walked?
Lee Sungkook was the first to shout.
“Oh, isn’t that it?”
There really was an old shrine nearby.
Gwanseongmyo’s Southern Shrine.
A shrine like this in the middle of the city?
The description beside the shrine surprised me even more.
Huh, could this really be?
It was a shrine to someone I hadn’t expected at all.
Who would have thought there would be a shrine honoring one of China’s greatest gods of war (武神) in a place like this?
Yoo Sangah asked with a nervous expression.
“What should we do now······?”
I looked around. There was no idol in sight.
“Let’s pay our respects first.”
This was different from the time with Samyeongdang. Recklessly wreaking havoc didn’t always earn a good reward.
We set out an offering of water obtained nearby, then quietly pressed our palms together. How much time had passed? A system message sounded.
[This shrine has been neglected for a long time.]
[A constellation who favors the crescent blade is pleased by your visit.]
[A constellation who favors the crescent blade reveals its modifier.]
[The constellation ‘Lord of the Beautiful Beard, Marquis Zhuangmou’ bestows a blessing upon you.]
Lord of the Beautiful Beard (美 髯公), Marquis Zhuangmou (壯繆侯).
A Chinese god of war, but a historical figure everyone in Korea knew too.
Because this constellation was none other than Guan Yu (關羽), courtesy name Yunchang (雲長), from Romance of the Three Kingdoms.
[The constellation’s blessing increases your Strength and Constitution stats by 5 each for the next 24 hours.]
Lee Sungkook spoke, his face lighting up.
“Holy shit······ Representative-nim, haven’t we hit the jackpot?”
“It’s a decent start.”
I didn’t know why Seoul had a shrine to Guan Yu, but Japan had shrines honoring the Duke of Loyalty and Warfare too, so perhaps it wasn’t so strange.
Guan Yu Yunchang was at least as famous worldwide as the Duke of Loyalty and Warfare, so a buff of this magnitude was only natural. Still.
“It seems we won’t be able to get an item here.”
“That’s a shame. It would’ve been nice to get something like the Green Dragon Crescent Blade······.”
In fact, even if there had been an idol, he was a Chinese historical figure, so there was no way a good item would turn up in Korea.
Who was the incarnation in China who had obtained Guan Yu again······?
Guan Yu was no match for the Great Sage, Heaven’s Equal or Uriel, but obtaining someone like Guan Yu would be enough to become the dominant power in a region of China.
Lee Gilyoung grabbed my collar.
“Hyung.”
A cockroach’s antennae moving furiously.
I had a bad feeling, and then I saw a crowd marching in formation in the distance.
Roughly fifty.

Their average Constitution, Strength, and Agility, as detected by [Calm Observation], were around 40. They fell far short of the <Apostles>, but were good enough to be called a respectable elite force.
A warlord traveling with fifty elite troops.
Lee Sungkook muttered.
“Those outfits, somewhere······.”
Men in historical-drama costumes that evoked the hwarang.
Every one of them had powder on his face, and anyone could see that they were exceptionally handsome. Those guys would never become slaves even if they met the Tyrant King.
Lee Sungkook whispered.
“Isn’t that man in the front row Hwang Sungmin? They look like celebrities.”
Anyone watching might have thought it was a historical-drama shoot, but what radiated from them was unmistakable killing intent. A man stepped forward, pointed his spear at me, and demanded.
“Who dares block the king’s path?”
“And who are you?”
I had a rough idea, but I asked anyway.
I had thought we would encounter them a little later. This was sooner than expected.
A woman’s voice came from among the hwarang.
“That brown flag······ could you be a ‘king’ too?”
“···I am. Why?”
“I never imagined there would be a ‘king’ in Jung-gu too. How surprising.”
Her voice was like flower petals brushing past in a spring breeze.
To be precise, though, it was probably a voice she’d put on for effect.
I answered.
“Kings are commonplace in this world now.”
“Even in a world where kings are commonplace, not just anyone can become one. Everyone, fall back!”

The hwarang ranks parted in perfect order, revealing a woman in royal attire at their center. Her luxuriant hair was swept into an elegant updo. She was beautiful enough to pass for the heroine of just about any historical drama.
“I-isn’t that Min Jiwon?”
Lee Sungkook stammered. The woman smiled.
“It seems someone recognizes me?”
“I-I was a fan!”
Dazed and entranced, Lee Sungkook took a step forward.
Idiot.
He was supposed to be a [Hypnotist]. What was he doing getting entranced first?
[Activating the exclusive skill, ‘Destroy Evil Lv.2’!]
Lee Sungkook, whose eyes had been losing focus, immediately came to his senses.
“Ah, I-I’m sorry.”
A curious glint flashed in the woman’s eyes.
This was interesting, though.
The fact that Lee Sungkook recognized her meant this woman called ‘Min Jiwon’ had existed in reality.
...The ‘King of Beauty (美戱王),’ one of Seoul’s Seven Kings, was a real person?
It felt a little strange. Because ‘Min Jiwon’ was also the real name of the ‘King of Beauty,’ a character in ‘Ways of Survival.’
Was it just a coincidence?
Well, I’d find out if I checked.
[Activating the exclusive skill ‘Character List’!]
Fortunately, the skill activated without trouble.
<Character Information>
Name: Min Jiwon
Age: 26
Constellation Sponsor (背後星): Supreme Maegum (寐錦之尊)
Exclusive Attributes: Actor (Rare), Queen of Tragedy (Hero)
Exclusive Skills: [Weapons Training Lv.5], [Army Command Lv.2], [Peach Blossom Charm Lv.4], [Skin Enhancement Lv.1], [Thousand Faces Lv.3], [Acting Lv.2]······.
Stigmas: [Heavenly Charm (天人魅惑) Lv.4], [Exceptional Heroine Lv.3]
Overall Stats: [Constitution Lv.18], [Strength Lv.18], [Agility Lv.21], [Magic Power Lv.23]

Overall Evaluation: An outstanding constellation sponsor has met an outstanding incarnation. Her exquisite beauty will shine all the brighter under her sponsor’s protection. As long as her beauty does not fade, her army will remain loyal to her alone.
As expected, this woman was the King of Beauty from the original ‘Ways of Survival.’
Judging by how [Character List] activated immediately, she didn’t seem to be a real person······ so how had Lee Sungkook recognized her?
Could it have something to do with Lee Sungkook being registered in the character dictionary?
